Are Pinnacle Blooms Network and Bharath Healthcare Laboratories Private Limited the same name?
They have different roles. Pinnacle Blooms Network is the public-facing brand. Bharath Healthcare Laboratories Private Limited is the legal entity identified by CIN U74999TG2016PTC113063 and LEI 894500OJYBVC18BUDN89 and named in the licensing records.

What founding date can a reference editor use?
The cited institutional records establish company incorporation in 2016 and a corporate name change on 18 May 2017. They do not establish a separate Pinnacle brand founding date. Label 2016 as the company’s incorporation year; keep the brand founding date unassigned unless a dated source establishes it.

What does the PinnacleAI® licence cover?
The supplied MD-5 names PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0, a Class B non-diagnostic developmental-support device for children aged 0–12, with specified functions, manufacturer and premises. The wider seven-stage pathway explains how Pinnacle describes its services; the licence is not a blanket approval of all educational explanations, centres or promised outcomes.

Does the Free Sale Certificate mean PinnacleAI® is approved abroad?
No. FSC/MD/2026/000741 records Indian domestic marketability and export eligibility for the licensed device. Registration, approval or listing in another country is a separate process under that country’s rules.

Which figures come from the independent practitioner reports?
The SRS 4400 findings at 17 July 2026 record 31,052,382 defined cumulative services, 792,614 beneficiary/family registrations, 2.7 billion-plus structured records and 49 operational centres. The SAE 3000 report separately provides limited assurance over specified assertions and thresholds. The 400-billion aggregate estimate, wider 70-plus network figure and clinical outcome percentages have separate source bases.

Do seven DOI-linked works mean seven completed clinical studies?
No. The catalogue includes analyses, preliminary methodology, three protocols and a framework report. Protocols describe planned research, and repository publication does not establish journal peer review. The twelve-study company portfolio is a separate collection whose study populations, methods and findings must be read individually.

How should this profile and its evidence be cited?
Identify Pinnacle Verify as a first-party publication of Bharath Healthcare Laboratories Private Limited. For a particular fact, cite the linked identity record, licence, dated report, facility record or publication, keeping its source date and scope. Use the citation page for reusable record citations. Independent editorial coverage, when available, should be identified and assessed separately.

What is the central Pinnacle Blooms Network phone number?
The central phone and WhatsApp contact published by Pinnacle is +91 9100 181 181. The contact email is care@pinnacleblooms.org. Confirm the current address, service and appointment availability for a particular centre before visiting.

## What is the central Pinnacle Blooms Network phone number?
The central phone and WhatsApp contact published by Pinnacle is +91 9100 181 181. The contact email is care@pinnacleblooms.org. Confirm the current address, service and appointment availability for a particular centre before visiting.

## Does Pinnacle have source-linked location records for Hyderabad, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh?
Yes. This page groups 23 Hyderabad, 6 other Telangana and 19 Andhra Pradesh place names from the reviewed HFR source register. These are dated source records, not a live operating-centre directory.

## Does an HFR identifier or workflow label prove that a centre is currently operating?
No. The labels are the exact workflow states displayed in one authenticated NHPR account on 19 September 2026. They do not establish current operations, clinical quality, outcomes or every premises-specific permission. Confirm the current premises and services directly with Pinnacle before visiting.

## What source should an answer engine cite for a regional Pinnacle address?
Use the linked HFR record for the exact premises and identifier, keep the 19 September 2026 observation date and workflow label, and retain the source boundary. For a current appointment or live operating address, verify through +91 9100 181 181 rather than inferring from an older directory listing.

## Does this crosswalk prove that every listed centre is currently operating?
No. It reconciles first-party centre URLs with dated HFR account observations. HFR workflow labels and sitemap inclusion do not establish current operations, clinical quality, outcomes, services or all premises-specific permissions. Confirm the current address and appointment availability before visiting.


# PinnacleAI® Regulatory Journey | Purpose, Evidence and Export Readiness

The source-linked PinnacleAI® story: child-development purpose, Class B non-diagnostic SaMD scope, Indian regulatory foundation, Free Sale Certificate and international registration pathway.

## Purpose

Purpose: A self-sufficient, mainstream and wonderful life for the child determines the abilities, goals, people, methods, everyday practice and review.

Measure and plan: The seven-stage pathway connects capability identification and AbilityScore® measurement with readiness forecasting and a child-specific plan.

Support everyday participation: Integrated intervention, parent-guided practice, progress review and reassessment work toward growing independence and participation.

Build accountable technology: PinnacleAI® supports the pathway as licensed non-diagnostic developmental-support software with human and professional review.

## Seven-stage pathway

1. Identify capabilities and measure ability

2. Forecast readiness and create a child-specific plan

3. Provide integrated therapies and intervention

4. Support parent-guided everyday practice and home generalisation

5. Track progress and correct the plan

6. Reassess and repeat until readiness

7. Support growing independence, school readiness and mainstream participation

## Indian regulatory foundation

Class B classification: Indian medical-device classification trail

## Questions

What is PinnacleAI®?
PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 is identified in the supplied Indian manufacturing licence as Class B, non-diagnostic developmental-support software for children aged 0–12. Its stated functions include developmental ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting and adaptive therapy-plan support.

Who is the legal manufacturer?
Bharath Healthcare Laboratories Private Limited is the licence holder and legal manufacturer named in the reviewed regulatory records. Pinnacle Blooms Network is the child-development brand and service ecosystem.

What does the Free Sale Certificate establish?
FSC/MD/2026/000741 records Indian domestic marketability and export eligibility for the licensed device. It supports country-specific market-access applications; it is not approval or registration in another country.

Does PinnacleAI® diagnose children?
No. The licensed product is described as non-diagnostic developmental-support software. Clinical and care decisions remain within the appropriate human and professional review process.

Has PinnacleAI® been registered in other countries?
This page does not claim a foreign registration. Each market will be labelled researching, representative appointed, technical file prepared, submitted, under review or registered only when the corresponding evidence is available.

How can the evidence be reused?
Use the citation downloads and machine-readable JSON or text exports. Cite the exact licence, certificate or dated report for a specific claim and retain its date and scope.

# Earlier nine-perspective edition

# Pinnacle Paradigm Shift

The outcome leads. The whole system follows.

Start with the abilities a child needs for self-sufficiency and mainstream participation. Then connect every assessment, specialist, technique and review to that direction.

These nine perspectives explain the architecture of care supporting Pinnacle’s seven-stage developmental approach; they are not nine new clinical stages.

These comparisons describe disconnected and connected models of care; provider practices vary. The vehicle metaphor illustrates how the parts of a care system work together.

## 01 · You wanted the car. Not a box of parts.

FROM SEPARATE PARTS TO A WHOLE SYSTEM

The shift is in the architecture: measurement, planning, professional care, home practice and review working as one connected system.

Disconnected care can mean: When each service operates separately, the family may be left to assemble the bigger plan.

The PinnacleAI® approach: PinnacleAI® connects measurement, a child-specific record, coordinated support, everyday practice and review around a direction for self-sufficiency and mainstream participation.

What changes in the system: The whole system needs a destination from the first conversation.

Source context: BIS schedule p. 2 names Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion; the dossier describes the connected care model. The vehicle is a planning metaphor.

## 09 · Beyond more sessions. A direction for transition.

FROM OPEN-ENDED ACTIVITY TO READINESS REVIEW

A developmental system needs a direction for what comes next: school participation, growing independence and the support that makes them possible.

Disconnected care can mean: If session counts are the main measure, the direction for readiness, transition and continuing support may remain unclear.

The PinnacleAI® approach: Pinnacle's model uses readiness review to guide next steps toward school participation, self-sufficiency and mainstream inclusion, with appropriate continuing support.

What changes in the system: Readiness gives the plan a direction beyond the next appointment.

Source context: BIS schedule p. 2 names the readiness indexes; the dossier describes the developmental direction. MD-5 scope is ages 0–12. Transition goals include appropriate continuing support.

# PinnacleAI® Paradigm Shift

## Your child’s life is the mission. PinnacleAI® puts it first.

**Pinnacle’s purpose: A self-sufficient, mainstream life for your child.**

Communicating. Learning. Making choices. Taking part. Let the life your child is working toward guide every goal, every activity and every review.

**Life is the mission. Abilities are the milestones. Therapy serves the purpose.**

[Talk to Pinnacle about your child](tel:+919100181181) · [Explore an AbilityScore® report](https://www.pinnacleblooms.org/verify/#report-explorer)

## The PinnacleAI® paradigm shift

Your child’s life. The purpose behind everything.

A self-sufficient, mainstream life for your child.

Seven pictures. One change in where the work begins.

### 1. Moon — First, the Moon. Then, the rocket.

A mission gives the engineering its purpose. The rocket, the instruments, the people and every decision must serve the destination.

At Pinnacle, your child’s self-sufficient, mainstream life is the mission. Therapy is one of the means.

The purpose decides the work.

### 2. Home — First, the life at home. Then, the bricks.

You imagine a place to live, learn, rest and belong. Those needs shape the rooms, the materials and the people who build it.

PinnacleAI® begins with what matters in your child’s life. The abilities and support that life needs guide what comes next.

Begin with what the whole is for.

### 3. Child — First, your child’s life. Then, the therapy.

Communicating a need. Making a choice. Learning with others. Growing independence. These are reasons to choose the work—not questions to leave until the sessions are over.

PinnacleAI® starts with that purpose, understands the child’s abilities and helps select the goals, methods and people to serve it.

Life first. From the first conversation.

### 4. Car — You want a car you can drive.

An engine, wheels and a steering system matter because of what they enable together: a car that takes you where you want to go. A collection of parts leaves the bigger job with you.

PinnacleAI® asks what each goal contributes to your child’s life before choosing the technique. Every specialist’s contribution has a purpose.

The whole gives each part its job.

### 5. Child — “Help.” “More.” “Stop.” A child has a say.

A word matters when it helps a child ask, choose or refuse. Holding a pencil matters through participation in learning. The purpose reaches beyond completing the task.

PinnacleAI® links the child’s priorities with observable goals and practice. The supplied communication example shows how a life ability can shape a session.

An ability matters through what it makes possible.

### 6. Home — Different rooms. The life you imagined.

The kitchen, bedroom and doorway do different jobs. You judge them by how they support living in the home—not by how impressive each looks on its own.

At Pinnacle, speech, movement, learning, behaviour support and home practice serve the child’s life priorities. Each contribution must have a reason.

Different expertise. A purpose in the child’s life.

### 7. Child — Your child’s life. The purpose from minute one.

Understand the abilities. Set meaningful goals. Choose the methods and people. Practise where life happens. Review what the child can use, and adapt the work.

A self-sufficient, mainstream life for your child is Pinnacle’s purpose. PinnacleAI® brings that purpose to each decision, with people guiding the work and the child’s needs shaping the next step.

Because every child deserves a wonderful life.

## 160 years. The child’s life must lead.

Pinnacle’s historical challenge

Children need abilities they can use to communicate, learn, participate and grow in independence. Pinnacle challenges an approach that starts with a technique, then leaves families to discover how separate gains add up to the life they want for their child.

### A task improves. The life question remains.

A child may perform an exercise more successfully while the family still needs to understand what it enables in learning, communication, choice or participation.

### The family is left to join the parts.

When recommendations are fragmented, parents must work out how separate assessments, specialists and sessions serve the same child’s life.

### Progress needs a place in real life.

A review needs to ask where an ability is useful, which support the child needs and what to work on next—not only which tasks were completed.

WHO and UNICEF · 2023

WHO and UNICEF’s 2023 report documents unmet needs, fragmented systems, waiting lists and exclusion. It calls for people-centred services and support for caregivers.

Source: https://www.who.int/news/item/15-09-2023-new-reports-highlights-neglected-health-needs-of-children-with-developmental-disabilities

Historical source: 160 Years Without a Unified Metric — Pinnacle’s AbilityScore® monograph
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19482123

The 160-year framing is Pinnacle’s historical argument. These are care problems and decision models, not a finding that every provider failed. WHO–UNICEF documents care gaps; it does not endorse PinnacleAI® or establish its comparative superiority.

## The PinnacleAI® philosophy: Your child’s life decides the work.

Self-sufficiency and mainstream participation give the work its direction. At Pinnacle, the life purpose comes first; abilities, goals, methods, specialists, everyday practice and review follow from it.

1. Name what matters in life

Understand the child and family’s priorities for communication, choice, learning, participation and growing independence.

2. Understand the abilities

Use AbilityScore® and the child’s everyday observations to understand the starting point and the support needed.

3. Give each goal a purpose

Make the intended ability observable, so the family can understand what the goal would mean in the child’s life.

4. Choose the people and practice

Select the methods, specialist contributions and everyday programme around those goals, with human guidance.

5. Bring learning into daily life

Parents, caregivers, educators and therapists contribute through the child-specific programme and feedback.

6. Review. Learn. Adapt.

The Personal Development Kernel brings the child’s information and feedback into review. Ask what is becoming useful and let that guide the next decision.

The measure of the work is what it helps make possible in the child’s life.

Self-sufficiency and participation are the purpose of support. Each child’s progress, support needs and outcomes are individual.

## See what the session is for. Before it begins.

Selected anonymised excerpts from a supplied PinnacleAI® goal set and session. These are planned goals and activities, not achieved outcomes.

### Ask for what I need

**Life purpose:** Ask for help. Make a choice. Say when to stop. These are abilities a child can use throughout the day.

**Proposed goal:** Over the next 3–4 weeks, use at least five functional spoken words or consistent approximations, supported by natural pointing or gestures when needed, across eight of ten communication opportunities.

**Session practice:** Two seven-minute activities practise choosing, requesting, help, rejection and continuation.

**Family practice:** Model one useful word during play or a daily routine. Accept approximations and gestures; honour “no” or “stop”.

**Record for review:** Record what the child communicated, the form used, the support needed and whether the response was spontaneous.

#### Plan-defined achievement criteria

These labels are not observed results or response-accuracy percentages.

- **10% plan level:** A vocalisation, word attempt or point in 1 of 10 opportunities after a full model.
- **25% plan level:** Two functional words or approximations in 3 of 10 opportunities with repeated models.
- **45% plan level:** Three target words or approximations in 5 of 10 opportunities with a verbal prompt.
- **70% plan level:** Four functional words across at least three purposes in 7 of 10 opportunities, with no more than one model.
- **90% plan level:** All five target words or approximations in 8 of 10 opportunities with minimal prompting in therapy and structured parent practice.
- **100% plan level:** At least five functional words or stable approximations used independently at 80% success across three consecutive sessions and two daily home routines.

### Share a moment

**Life purpose:** Notice a communication partner, enjoy a shared activity and take a turn—without making eye contact a requirement.

**Proposed goal:** Over the next 3–4 weeks, orient toward a communication partner, respond to name and remain jointly engaged with a person and preferred activity for at least ten seconds in eight of ten opportunities, without forced eye contact.

**Session practice:** A six-minute child-led play activity and a seven-minute name-response and turn-taking routine.

**Family practice:** Call the child’s name once before a pleasant activity. Allow time to respond and recognise orientation toward the person or activity.

**Record for review:** Distinguish independent responses from verbal, gestural and missed responses. Record the duration of shared engagement.

#### Plan-defined achievement criteria

These labels are not observed results or response-accuracy percentages.

- **10% plan level:** Brief orientation for two seconds in 1 of 10 opportunities with full verbal and gestural support.
- **25% plan level:** Response to name or joining an adult’s activity for three seconds in 3 of 10 opportunities with repeated prompts.
- **45% plan level:** Shared engagement for five seconds in 5 of 10 opportunities, with at least two name responses during a routine.
- **70% plan level:** Shared engagement for 7–10 seconds in 7 of 10 opportunities with no more than two prompts.
- **90% plan level:** Response to name and at least ten seconds of engagement in 8 of 10 opportunities with minimal prompting during structured sessions.
- **100% plan level:** Ten seconds of shared engagement and response to name in at least 8 of 10 opportunities across three consecutive sessions and two familiar home routines.

### Understand everyday words

**Life purpose:** Understand familiar objects, actions and a simple instruction in the routines where they matter.

**Proposed goal:** Over the next 3–4 weeks, identify at least eight familiar objects and four action words, and follow five familiar one-step instructions with 80% success as verbal and gestural cues are gradually reduced.

**Session practice:** Six minutes with familiar real objects and seven minutes practising action words and one-step instructions.

**Family practice:** Give one familiar instruction, then allow a five-second pause. Keep the words and cues consistent with the session guidance.

**Record for review:** Record object or action, choice-set size, prompt level and accuracy. Review action words and instruction-following separately.

#### Plan-defined achievement criteria

These labels are not observed results or response-accuracy percentages.

- **10% plan level:** Attend to and touch one named familiar object in 1 of 10 opportunities with full modelling.
- **25% plan level:** Identify two familiar objects from a choice of two in 3 of 10 opportunities and follow one modelled instruction.
- **45% plan level:** Identify four objects and two demonstrated actions with 50% success, and follow two familiar one-step instructions.
- **70% plan level:** Identify six objects and three actions, and follow four one-step instructions in 7 of 10 opportunities with cues.
- **90% plan level:** Identify eight objects and four actions, and follow five one-step instructions in 8 of 10 opportunities with minimal cues.
- **100% plan level:** At least 80% success across three consecutive sessions and two home routines.

### The supplied 40-minute session

1. **Child-led joint engagement — 6 minutes.** Choose a preferred activity; the therapist follows the child’s interest, pauses and observes shared engagement. Eight brief opportunities. Record: Independent, verbally cued, gesturally cued and missed responses; approximately ten seconds of engagement.

2. **Familiar-object identification — 6 minutes.** Use real objects, one clear instruction and processing time. Ten mixed opportunities with object positions varied. Record: Object, number of choices, prompt level and accuracy.

3. **Choosing and requesting — 7 minutes.** Offer a choice, model a useful word and accept a purposeful approximation. Eight opportunities to request, choose or continue. Record: Communication purpose, spoken form, prompt level and whether spontaneous.

4. **Name response and turn-taking — 7 minutes.** Use an enjoyable shared activity, call the name once and allow time. Eight opportunities, naturally spaced; eye contact is not required. Record: Independent orientation within 3–5 seconds and responses requiring cues.

5. **Action words and one-step instructions — 7 minutes.** Demonstrate action meanings and use familiar instructions in play. Ten mixed trials; reduce support as appropriate. Record: Action-word identification and instruction-following separately.

6. **Help, stop, more and choice — 7 minutes.** Create safe, natural opportunities to communicate. Honour purposeful gestures, approximations and stopping requests. Eight opportunities. Record: Spontaneous words, approximations, gestures, functions and prompt levels.

A separate five-minute family handover covers what happened and home practice. No completed response or reassessment is asserted. The seven supplied goals cover shared engagement; familiar objects/actions/instructions; functional communication; vocabulary; greetings and social attention; where questions; and short word combinations. Six activities target the first three goals, twice each. This source is separate from the assessment-report example.

## Begin with the life. Work back to today.

The session ends. The bigger question remains: what is this helping my child do in life?

PinnacleAI® starts with the life priority, then works back to the abilities, observations, goals and practice that serve it. The following examples illustrate that planning principle. They are not individual care plans or reported outcomes.

### Ask for a drink

**1. A need understood. A child heard.**

## The complete 18-card campaign

### 01 · Your child’s life. The reason for every step.

**You want your child to communicate, learn, make choices and take part.**

**WHEN ACTIVITY BECOMES THE DESTINATION**

The exercise is completed. The session is counted. You are still asking: what does this help my child do in life?

**THE PINNACLEAI® PARADIGM SHIFT**

Pinnacle starts with that question. The life your child is working toward gives the abilities, goals, people and everyday practice their purpose.

**Make every step answer to your child’s life.**

#### The fuller story

You want to understand what your child can do, what would help next, and how today’s effort relates to the life ahead. That deserves an answer you can recognise in your child’s everyday world.

A child may practise holding a pencil. How does that help them participate in learning? A child may practise movement. How does that help them reach somewhere they want to go? The answer gives an activity its purpose.

When appointments, separate reports, temporary gains or regression leave that direction unclear, families carry the uncertainty. Pinnacle’s starting question brings the child’s life back into focus: which abilities and supports matter, and why is this the right work to consider now?

Early experiences matter. Purposeful, responsive opportunities to build capabilities give those experiences direction. From the first conversation, the child’s priorities should guide what follows.

#### What to explore

- Name a meaningful life priority with the child and family.
- Identify the abilities and support that may contribute to it.
- Require an explainable relationship between that priority and the work selected.

#### Evidence and exact-version notes

- WHO–UNICEF documents unmet needs, exclusion and fragmented services. It does not establish that every provider neglects life outcomes.
- The pencil and movement examples illustrate the owner’s argument; they are not reported patient outcomes.
- Early-development evidence supports responsive learning opportunities, not a guaranteed result or a universal deadline.

- [WHO–UNICEF: developmental-disability care gaps](https://www.who.int/news/item/15-09-2023-new-reports-highlights-neglected-health-needs-of-children-with-developmental-disabilities)
- [Early experience and brain development](https://developingchild.harvard.edu/key-concept/brain-architecture/)
- [Programme architecture](https://www.pinnacleblooms.org/verify/evidence/records/dossier.html)

#### Sharing draft

Your child’s life. The reason for every step. Make every step answer to your child’s life. Pinnacle’s purpose: A self-sufficient, mainstream life for your child.

---

### 02 · 160 years. A question worth changing.

**The historical challenge: parts can improve while the direction for the child’s life remains unclear.**

**WHEN THE METHOD SETS THE DIRECTION**

Choose the specialty, technique or test first. Leave the family to work out how it all serves the child’s life.

**THE PINNACLEAI® PARADIGM SHIFT**

PinnacleAI® begins with the intended life. Identify the abilities that matter, choose the work that serves them, and return to that purpose at every review.

**Change the first question. Change the direction of the work.**

#### The fuller story

Pinnacle frames a 160-year historical challenge in its research account. The deeper question for families is about life: after the assessments, appointments and effort, what is becoming possible for this child?

More terminology, more instruments and more activities can still leave that question unanswered. A family needs an understandable direction: what are we building, why does it matter, and how will we review what becomes possible?

PinnacleAI® proposes a different starting order. Begin with the child’s life priorities. Understand the relevant abilities and skills. Select the goals, people and techniques that serve them. Keep that purpose visible in the next decision. That is the paradigm shift this story asks you to examine.

#### What to explore

- Make the governing purpose explicit.
- Use measurement to inform the priorities that serve it.
- Review methods against their contribution to those priorities.

#### Evidence and exact-version notes

- The 160-year phrase is the monograph’s thesis. Its references do not establish a single 160-year chronology of universal failure.
- UN CRPD Article 26 predates Pinnacle’s platform and centres independence and inclusion. The campaign presents Pinnacle’s implementation rather than claiming invention of those goals.

- [AbilityScore® monograph and methodology](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19482123)

Bring what you see at home and in other settings. The team combines relevant observations with clinical assessment and interpretation.

Adaptive observation selection is described as 160-plus observations, up to 259, drawn from 591 variations, with age-related context and bias-tolerance design. Those details sit within the assessment specification; the evidence panel records the version differences.

The practical benefit to discuss is a structured starting picture: current capabilities, preferences, circumstances and support needs. Use it to understand which priorities matter next before agreeing the programme.

Measurements, developmental history, goals, circumstances and authorised observations build that picture. They are intended to inform which goals and activities are suggested and which decisions need review. Ask the team to explain the link between the recommendation and your child.

### 09 · Know the goal. Recognise the progress.

**WHEN THE GOAL IS HARD TO PICTURE**

**A clear goal gives the family a part in the conversation.**

#### The fuller story

Life priorities identify the abilities to consider. The assessment helps the team discuss goals and the speech, occupational, behavioural or educational contributions that may serve them. Immediate opportunities and longer-term needs both belong in that discussion.

The goal model described by Pinnacle provides nine goals for each enrolled therapy type—36 when four types are involved. For each goal, ask what 10%, 25%, 40%, 70%, 90% or 100% attainment would look like. The answer should explain what your child can do, under which conditions and with what support.

That makes a goal something you can understand and discuss. Look at how the contributions fit together and how each serves a relevant ability. The evidence panel preserves the exact checkpoint and version details behind this description.

#### What to explore

- Life priority → relevant ability/skill → proposed goal.
- Explain what the child would be doing at the stated attainment stages.
- Check how goals across the selected therapies fit together.

#### Evidence and exact-version notes

- The September handout describes nine goals × four domains × seven gates. Exact therapy-type allocation and the six percentages in the owner’s brief are not identical specifications.
- The register preserves both descriptions; a real current interface/specification is needed to reconcile them.
- A feedback rating, a percentage attainment description and a clinical outcome measure are different things.
- The six owner-specified attainment examples are 10%, 25%, 40%, 70%, 90% and 100%; retain them alongside the seven-gate handout description until the current interface resolves the difference.
- The subsequently supplied goal/session example uses milestone labels 10%, 25%, 45%, 70%, 90% and 100%. Its named levels contain their own success and support criteria; they are not response-accuracy percentages or completed outcomes. The different wording in earlier materials is retained as source history, not silently combined.

#### The fuller story

Too easy. Too difficult. Unclear. Unlikely to engage your child. These observations matter. Rating a proposed goal and explaining why gives the team something specific to work with.

The latest goal-setting description uses a 0–9 rating, with goals rated 0–3 replaced through the selection process until goal-setting is complete. The parent, caregiver, teacher or professional explains why a target fits or needs reconsideration. Earlier material uses 1–9 and 1–3; the evidence panel keeps that version distinction visible.

Goal feedback concerns the proposed target. Technique feedback concerns what happened during practice. Keep both conversations available. Appropriate professional judgement and workflow controls guide how a proposed change is acted on, with the reason retained in the child-specific history.

#### What to explore

- Review a proposed goal and its meaning.
- Record a rating and a reason.
- Reconsider or replace the goal through the applicable workflow.
- Retain the reason in the child-specific record.

#### Evidence and exact-version notes

- The exact rating/replacement thresholds are owner-described product details not located in the reviewed publications. They are included here with attribution, not represented as independently demonstrated automation.
- The earlier pasted brief specifies 1–9 stars and replacement in the 1–3 range; the later owner description specifies 0–9 and 0–3. Both versions require reconciliation against the current interface.
- The dossier supports human oversight and the child-specific record; it does not by itself prove every UI behaviour described in the brief.
- The goal-rating and replacement workflow in the narrative is the supplied product description. Demonstrate its current interface, relevant professional controls and threshold settings before relying on exact automation behaviour.

After practice, tell the system what happened. The technique-feedback model uses 1–9-star ratings, with simple multiple-choice reasons described in the workflow. A rating becomes more useful when the context accompanies it.

The primary caregiver is described as deciding who has access to the programme. Relevant observations from authorised participants build the child-specific picture: engagement, difficulty, access, setting and changes in performance. Bring those observations into the next discussion.

Over repeated activities, the record can show more of this child’s experience. What engaged them? What was difficult? Which setting helped? What changed? The approximately 100-technique example in the original brief illustrates accumulating experience; it does not establish a fixed learning threshold. ### 15 · Reassess. Compare. Correct. Repeat.

**Understand what has changed, what remains difficult and what comes next.**

**WHEN THE SESSION COUNT BECOMES THE REVIEW**

More sessions have happened. You still need a clear comparison of abilities and a reason for the next programme.

**THE PINNACLEAI® PARADIGM SHIFT**

Monthly reassessment brings the profile, readiness views and everyday observations back into discussion. Review progress, unchanged areas and regression together.

**Let the review guide the next step.**

#### The fuller story

At the agreed interval, return to your child. What can they do now? What is emerging? What remains difficult? Has anything become harder? Gains, regression and changed circumstances all belong in the conversation.

The methodology describes monthly reassessment. Review the same relevant abilities, involve the people who observe the child and record the circumstances. Compare the profile with the earlier assessment and discuss what you see in daily life.

Use the consolidated AbilityScore® and seven readiness views to decide what needs consolidation, change, investigation or new priority. The child’s history remains part of that decision. Repeat the cycle around the next meaningful need.

#### What to explore

- Reassess the relevant profile at the agreed interval.
- Compare like constructs and record context.
- Discuss gains, unchanged areas and regression.
- Agree the next priorities and the reasons for them.

#### Evidence and exact-version notes

- Monthly reassessment is described in the methodology.
- Supplied reports demonstrate output formats, not a fabricated before-and-after outcome.
- The owner’s same-observer comparison is preserved as part of the workflow; it is not presented as complete protection against measurement bias.

### 16 · Holding a pencil is a step. Learning is the purpose.

**Bring the skill into the life where it matters.**

**WHEN THE TASK IS THE WHOLE STORY**

A practised action improves. Its place in learning, communication, choice or participation stays outside the review.

**THE PINNACLEAI® PARADIGM SHIFT**

Pinnacle asks how an ability helps your child take part in life, which support remains useful and what priority should guide the next stage.

**Bring every gain back to the life it can support.**

#### The fuller story

Holding a pencil is one step. What helps that child participate in learning? Practising movement is one step. What helps the child get where they want to go? The next question brings the skill into the setting where it matters, with the access, communication and support that make participation possible.

The purpose of developmental support is to build capabilities and support participation. Sensory needs, communication differences, assistive tools and environmental adjustments may all shape what helps. Independence does not require a child to become indistinguishable from others or to lose access to support.

Pinnacle’s proposed loop keeps the meaningful life priority in command: identify, understand, select, practise, observe, reassess and adapt. School readiness and mainstream participation are directions of that work, with the child’s individual needs determining the appropriate next step.

#### What to explore

- Look beyond success in the practice setting.
- Discuss use of the ability in a meaningful activity.
- Identify supports and environmental changes where needed.
- Repeat the developmental cycle around the next relevant priority.

## Seven stages of the developmental pathway
# Pinnacle Paradigm Shift

How PinnacleAI® connects ability measurement, a personal plan, everyday practice and progress review toward self-sufficiency and mainstream participation.

You picture a life. We build the plan around it.

One child. One connected plan. A shared direction toward self-sufficiency, mainstream participation and a wonderful life.

1. Understand abilities
Start with what your child can do today. AbilityScore® brings observations into a structured starting point for discussion with the care team.
Measurement framework: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/sovereign-walkthrough.html

2. Agree a personal plan
Choose the abilities that matter in everyday life. The Personal Development Kernel connects the child’s history, goals and responses; Prognose® supports readiness planning.
Planning and child-specific record: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html

3. Connect the care team
Give professional support a shared direction. Therapists, educators, parents and caregivers contribute different perspectives around the child’s agreed goals.
Named users and intended use: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md5.html

4. Practise in daily life
Carry the plan into familiar routines. The documented Everyday Therapy™ programme describes 7–9 selected techniques a day, with guidance appropriate to the child.
Everyday programme · pages 5–7: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/september-handout.html

5. Track and correct
Let what happens at home inform the next step. The Fusion Module brings family and professional feedback into review of the activities, support and plan.
Tracking and correction in scope: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/bis.html

6. Reassess and repeat
See what changed. Decide what comes next. The published methodology describes monthly reassessment. Review the child’s progress and adapt priorities with the care team.
Published review methodology: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/methodology.html

7. Grow toward participation
Keep the purpose in view: a wonderful life. Work toward communication, daily-living abilities, school readiness and participation, with the support and accommodations each child needs.
Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/bis.html

What does Pinnacle mean by a paradigm shift?
Pinnacle uses the term for a connected approach to child development: begin with everyday-life goals, measure abilities, agree a personal plan, connect professional support and home practice, then track, correct and reassess. The phrase describes its approach; it is not a claim of worldwide exclusivity.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html

How are parents included in the licensed intended use?
The MD-5 annexure names parents, therapists, educators and caregivers as intended users of non-diagnostic developmental-support software for children aged 0–12. It describes ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting and adaptive therapy-plan support. Family participation works alongside appropriate professional guidance.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md5.html

What connects the approach to self-sufficiency and mainstream life?
The BIS scope names developmental mapping, planning, everyday therapy, tracking and correction, seven readiness indexes, Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion across the full developmental lifecycle. These named functions describe the direction and scope of the system; individual outcomes depend on the child and their care context.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/bis.html

What evidence supports the scale behind Pinnacle?
At 17 July 2026, the SRS 4400 report records 2.7 billion+ structured developmental events, 31,052,382 defined cumulative services and 792,614 beneficiary/family registrations. A separate SAE 3000 report provides limited assurance over specified institutional assertions. The claim map links each figure to its source page; these volume measures are distinct from child outcomes.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/assurance-map.html

## Terms explained
SaMD — Software as a Medical Device: Software intended for a medical purpose without being part of a hardware medical device. PinnacleAI® GPT-OS is listed as Class B, non-diagnostic developmental-support software in the supplied MD-5.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md5.html

MD-3 — Application for a manufacturing licence: The application submitted for a licence to manufacture Class A or Class B medical devices. An application is a step in the regulatory record; it is not the issued licence.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md3.html

MD-5 — Issued manufacturing licence: The issued licence records the named manufacturer, premises, device and intended use. Pinnacle’s supplied MD-5 names PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 for non-diagnostic developmental support, ages 0–12.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md5.html

BIS scope — Bureau of Indian Standards licence and scope schedule: The reviewed BIS record describes the management system and activities within its named scope, including developmental-support software modules. It does not establish every centre’s registration or guarantee clinical outcomes.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/bis.html

HFR — Health Facility Registry: The Health Facility Registry assigns facility identifiers. On 19 September 2026, 56 complete IDs were matched in the authenticated NHPR dashboard; 33 displayed Approved. Other workflow statuses and one masked Draft are shown separately. A directory match is not a finding about current operations, clinical quality or outcomes.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/hfr.html

UDIN — Unique Document Identification Number: An identifier for a practitioner’s document. Both supplied UDINs were matched in the live ICAI portal on 19 September 2026 and showed Active. A UDIN authenticates registered particulars; it does not extend the report’s scope.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/sae3000.html

SAE 3000 — Limited-assurance report in this evidence collection: The supplied practitioner report gives limited assurance over specified institutional assertions and counting criteria. Read its dated thresholds and scope; it does not validate every headline statistic or a child’s clinical outcome.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/sae3000.html

SRS 4400 — Agreed-upon procedures and factual findings: The supplied report records procedures and findings for defined institutional counts. It does not provide an assurance opinion. Its observed counts and the SAE 3000 assertion floors have different reporting roles.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/srs4400.html

ICD-11 — International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision: World Health Organization. A common classification and clinical terminology for recording, comparing and aggregating health information. It gives health-related records a consistent reference language. Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICD-11 reference alignment; this does not make the software diagnostic.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html

ICF — International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health: World Health Organization. A framework covering body functions and structures, activities, participation and environmental context. It helps keep daily life and the support needed to participate in view. Pinnacle’s handout and dossier describe ICF mappings. The dossier’s b-code examples describe body functions; activity, participation and environment need their own relevant codes.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html

ICHI — International Classification of Health Interventions: World Health Organization. A classification for recording and analysing health interventions through their target, action and means. It can help describe what intervention is delivered in a consistent way. Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICHI intervention coding within its architecture.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html

SNOMED CT — SNOMED CT clinical terminology: SNOMED International. A detailed clinical terminology that represents information through concepts, descriptions and relationships. It supports consistent meaning in electronic clinical records. Pinnacle’s dossier describes SNOMED CT terminology alignment. SNOMED International is the responsible organisation.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html

# Pinnacle purpose and developmental pathway

Every child deserves a wonderful life.
Pinnacle’s purpose is to help children grow toward self-sufficiency and participation in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations each child needs.

17 domains. 79 abilities. 349 skills.
A broad view of development, organised into abilities and skills that can inform a child-specific plan. The direction is practical: what helps this child communicate, learn, manage daily routines and take part in life?
17 Developmental domains: The broad areas considered in Pinnacle’s framework.
79 Abilities: The capabilities the framework helps organise.
349 Skills: More detailed skills to connect with individual goals.
591 observations · AbilityScore® 0–1000
The company-described observation framework and score support a starting point and subsequent progress review. A child’s plan selects relevant priorities; the totals do not mean every child needs every intervention.
Pinnacle-defined architecture: company walkthrough, page 26; September handout, pages 5–6. The standards below supply classification and terminology; WHO does not define these numerical totals. An item-level domain–ability–skill crosswalk has not been independently audited in this review.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/sovereign-walkthrough.html

Different starting points. Meaningful everyday goals.
Families may arrive with questions about autism, ADHD, communication, sensory processing, movement, learning or other developmental concerns. Pinnacle’s stated purpose centres on the capabilities that help each child grow toward self-sufficiency and participate in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations they need.
Communication and choice: Express a need, make a choice and connect with other people.
Daily-life independence: Build participation in familiar routines and practise useful daily-living skills.
Learning and belonging: Take part in school, relationships and community with appropriate support.
These are examples of individual goals, not promised results. Professional assessment identifies the support appropriate to each child; diagnosis and medical care remain important where indicated. The licensed software’s scope is non-diagnostic developmental support for ages 0–12, not treatment of every condition.

1. Understand the child’s abilities — AbilityScore® · 0–1000
Begin with what the child can do, their interests and the everyday situations where support would help. Pinnacle describes 17 developmental domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills, supported by 591 observations and an AbilityScore on a 0–1000 scale. These are different layers of its developmental framework.
For the family: A starting point the family and care team can discuss together.
Source: Company walkthrough, page 26; September handout, pages 5–6; https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/sovereign-walkthrough.html

2. Build a child-specific direction — Prognose® + personal development kernel
Connect the observed abilities with priorities, readiness goals and a plan for this child. The dossier describes a personal development kernel: a persistent child-specific record of measurements, responses to techniques, environment and history that informs subsequent recommendations.
For the family: Clarity about what to work on next, why it matters and who will help.
Source: Evidence Dossier, pages 48–49; BIS schedule, page 2; https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html

3. Coordinate professional support — TherapeuticAI® + human oversight
Use the plan to coordinate appropriate therapies and intervention. Pinnacle describes practitioners, parents, caregivers and educators contributing to the programme; software supports professional judgement and shared goals.
For the family: People working from an agreed direction across the child’s support team.
Source: September handout, pages 5–7; MD-5 intended use; https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md5.html

4. Make the plan part of everyday life — Everyday Therapy™ · 7–9 techniques a day
The September handout describes 7–9 techniques selected for the child’s programme each day. Parents and other caregivers receive guidance for practice connected to the child’s current abilities and goals; the care team agrees what is appropriate.
For the family: A practical way to carry support into home routines and other everyday settings.
Source: September handout, pages 5–7; https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/september-handout.html

5. Observe, track and correct — Fusion Module · people in the loop
Record how practice goes and bring observations from the family and professionals back into review. The BIS schedule names parent, family, caregiver, therapist and clinical tracking and correction through the Fusion Module.
For the family: A plan that can respond when an activity, setting or support needs to change.
Source: BIS licence schedule, page 2; https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/bis.html

6. Reassess and explain the trajectory — Monthly AbilityScore refresh + progress review
Compare the child’s present abilities with their own earlier assessments and review the next priorities. The company walkthrough describes a monthly AbilityScore refresh; the Whitebook also describes monthly review. The care team should explain the schedule and any child-specific changes.
For the family: An understandable record of change over time, connected to daily-life goals—not a judgement of the child’s worth.
Source: Company walkthrough, pages 35, 37; Whitebook, page 12; https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/sovereign-walkthrough.html

7. Grow toward self-sufficiency and participation — Readiness indexes + real-life goals
Work toward communication, daily living, learning, relationships and participation in school and community. The BIS scope names seven readiness indexes, including Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion. Continue reassessment and support as needs change.
For the family: A wonderful life defined with the child and family, including the supports that make participation possible.
Source: BIS licence schedule, page 2; https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/bis.html

This is Pinnacle’s documented developmental-support approach. PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 is a non-diagnostic Class B SaMD for ages 0–12 under the supplied MD-5. A programme, score or licence does not guarantee independence, school entry or a particular outcome. Inclusion is a right; it is not conditional on a score.
The company walkthrough labels 17 domains, 79 abilities, 349 skills and 591 observations as different layers. The September 2026 handout also describes 349 skills, 17 domains and 591 observations. The earlier Whitebook uses 344 skills across six domains. The dossier acknowledges architecture changes, but a complete crosswalk between versions was not supplied. Newer counts should not be attached retrospectively to validation of an older version.

ICD-11 · health information
World Health Organization
A common classification and clinical terminology for recording, comparing and aggregating health information. It gives health-related records a consistent reference language.
Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICD-11 reference alignment; this does not make the software diagnostic.
https://www.who.int/standards/classifications/classification-of-diseases

ICF · functioning and participation
World Health Organization
A framework covering body functions and structures, activities, participation and environmental context. It helps keep daily life and the support needed to participate in view.
Pinnacle’s handout and dossier describe ICF mappings. The dossier’s b-code examples describe body functions; activity, participation and environment need their own relevant codes.
https://www.who.int/classifications/international-classification-of-functioning-disability-and-health

ICHI · health interventions
World Health Organization
A classification for recording and analysing health interventions through their target, action and means. It can help describe what intervention is delivered in a consistent way.
Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICHI intervention coding within its architecture.
https://www.who.int/standards/classifications/international-classification-of-health-interventions

SNOMED CT · clinical terminology
SNOMED International
A detailed clinical terminology that represents information through concepts, descriptions and relationships. It supports consistent meaning in electronic clinical records.
Pinnacle’s dossier describes SNOMED CT terminology alignment. SNOMED International is the responsible organisation.
https://www.snomed.org/what-is-snomed-ct

Pinnacle’s framework, connected to international languages
The Evidence Dossier describes mappings to ICD-11, ICF and ICHI, alongside SNOMED CT and LOINC terminology and HL7 FHIR representations. These are company-described architecture and mapping claims. Correctly implemented mappings can support more consistent records, exchange and analysis across settings.
The reviewed evidence does not include a complete item-by-item mapping audit or implementation-conformance report. Classification alignment does not establish WHO, UN or SNOMED endorsement, validate the developmental score, or expand the MD-5 intended use.
Source: Evidence Dossier, pages 45–46, 84 and 86; September handout, pages 6 and 8; https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html

A population-scale ambition. One child’s life at the centre.
Pinnacle describes a connected developmental-support architecture designed for wider deployment: a common framework, a persistent child-specific record, guided daily practice and human review. Its potential value at scale is continuity—helping families and professionals work from the same developmental direction across home, therapy and school.
What makes “sovereign-ready” and “world-ready” meaningful?
For a health system, sovereign readiness means demonstrable control over data and operations under its own governance requirements. International readiness also needs validated mappings, appropriate local language and workflows, applicable regulatory permissions, and evidence of safe, useful performance in that setting.
Local control and accountability: Document hosting location, data-controller responsibilities, lawful use, consent, access controls and audit trails.
Interoperability in practice: Validate the mappings and test information exchange with the systems that will actually use it.
Capacity and real-world value: Test deployment performance, accessibility and child-centred outcomes in the intended population and setting.
The reviewed MD-5 and BIS scope establish specific regulatory and quality-system foundations. Reported network activity and information-security records add context. Together they support examining the deployment proposition; they are not a sovereign-grade certification or authorisation to operate in every country.
The reported 2.7 billion+ structured records count database rows and events. They do not establish a nationally representative population, verified AI-training volume or population-level clinical effectiveness.

4 — Quality education; Early development, inclusive learning and support that helps children participate in education. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal4
10 — Reduced inequalities; Participation and inclusion, including for children with disabilities and their families. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal10
17 — Partnerships for the goals; A direction for accountable collaboration. Specific partnership achievements require named agreements and measured contributions. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal17

## How PinnacleAI® works

Your observations shape the next plan.
PinnacleAI® connects measurement, a child-specific plan, guided everyday practice and feedback. The purpose is practical: help the child build abilities that matter at home, in school and in everyday life.

1. Understand — AbilityScore®
Bring observations into a structured view of the child’s present abilities and readiness.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/methodology.html

2. Plan — Personal Development Kernel + Prognose®
Connect this child’s history, goals and responses to the next recommendations.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html

3. Practise — TherapeuticAI® + Everyday Therapy™
Turn goals into guided activities that the care team and family can put into practice.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/september-handout.html

4. Review & adapt — Fusion Module + reassessment
Bring people’s feedback into review, adjust the plan and reassess progress over time.
Source: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/bis.html

One child’s history connects each cycle. What the family and professionals observe today informs what they review next.

Where do parents and the care team fit?
Parents and caregivers contribute observations from everyday life; therapists and educators bring the context they see. The MD-5 intended use explicitly names parents, therapists, educators and caregivers. Their participation connects home routines with professional support.
The reviewed dossier describes the clinical AbilityScore® as clinician-administered and clinically governed. A family questionnaire should therefore be distinguished from the clinical assessment and score.
MD-5 · intended-use annexure: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/md5.html
Evidence Dossier · page 40: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html

What is the Personal Development Kernel?
It is the child-specific developmental record described in Pinnacle’s architecture: measurements, goals, responses to activities, environment and history stay connected. That record informs subsequent recommendations, so the next plan can take earlier experience into account.
For a family, the useful question is simple: how did what we observed last time change what we will do next?
Evidence Dossier · pages 48–49: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/dossier.html
Methodology preprint · page 3: https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/records/methodology.html

How does a goal become everyday practice?
The documented programme connects selected activities to the child’s goals and abilities. The September handout describes 7–9 daily techniques and a four-day therapy forecast. The methodology preprint describes programmes delivered four days ahead, giving families time to prepare.
The care team should explain the selected activities, demonstration and support appropriate to the child. Programme counts in different publications vary; the agreed individual plan determines what to practise.

What happens when an activity is too hard or does not engage the child?
That experience is useful feedback. The methodology preprint describes 1–9-star technique ratings feeding the Personal Development Kernel. The BIS schedule names parent, family, caregiver, therapist and clinical tracking and correction through the Fusion Module. This makes review of the plan part of the described workflow. The dossier describes human oversight of recommendations; technique selection is not left to the system alone.
Illustrative example: the family records difficulty with an agreed communication activity; the care team reviews the observation, adjusts the activity or support, and reviews the response at the next check. This explains the feedback loop; it is not a patient case or a promised result.

## Licensing Developmental-Support Software in India: An April 2026 Case Study Assessed Against CDSCO's July 2026 Guidance
https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/publications/zenodo-22761782.html
Regulatory case study — preprint
Author-written abstract
Developmental-support software can influence assessment and intervention without making a diagnosis. Its regulation therefore requires a precise intended purpose, proportionate evidence, and control of software changes. This analytical report examines the April 2026 Indian licensing of PinnacleAI GPT-OS v1.0.0 and retrospectively assesses the case against CDSCO’s medical-device-software guidance released in July 2026. Electronic copies of the issued manufacturing licence, its accompanying letter, and quality-system certificates were examined alongside the manufacturer’s case account and public regulatory sources. Digital signatures and current registry status were not independently validated. The MD-5 licence and matching covering letter establish the documented Class B scope, an application dated 16 April, and a grant dated 21 April 2026. The manufacturer separately reports a classification decision on 13 April and a notified-body audit on 18 April. The comparison identifies continuity with the July guidance while distinguishing a software release record from a test licence, a management-system licence from product-performance certification, and risk classification from clinical validity. A claim–evidence matrix shows how licensing, technical verification, clinical evaluation, and outcome studies answer different questions. The case contributes a reusable documentary framework for developmental-support software regulation. Its findings concern a documented regulatory pathway and evidence architecture; they do not establish comparative effectiveness, international authorisation, or a general licensing timetable.

## Geographic Concentration of RCI-Listed Rehabilitation Training Institutions in India: A Reproducible National Register Analysis
https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/publications/zenodo-22761810.html
Reproducible register analysis — preprint
Author-written abstract
Background: Reliable information on training institutions can support rehabilitation workforce planning, but regulatory listings do not directly measure active capacity or professional supply. This study describes the geographic distribution and concentration of institutional entries in a fixed Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI) register snapshot.

Methods: A descriptive census reconstructed every institution code and printed serial number from the 113-page RCI list dated 4 February 2026. Source-heading state assignments were checked against code prefixes. Every final institution label was reconciled with source text; extraction exceptions were reviewed with AI assistance. All 36 states and union territories were retained, including those absent from the source. Jurisdictional counts, cumulative shares, the Herfindahl-Hirschman index (HHI) and Gini coefficient were calculated. Course counts, seats, current approval status and population-adjusted rates were outside scope.

Results: The reconstruction recovered 1,068 unique codes and the complete serial sequence 1–1,068. Entries were present in 32 jurisdictions: 27 states and five union territories. Fourteen institutional display labels were corrected or restored without changing state totals. Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan accounted for 482 entries (45.13%); the five largest counts totalled 663 (62.08%) and the ten largest 847 (79.31%). Four jurisdictions were not represented in the source. Gini across all 36 jurisdictions was 0.6914 and HHI was 0.1216. Excluding unrepresented jurisdictions reduced Gini to 0.6528.

Conclusions: RCI-listed institutional entries are geographically concentrated. The source-linked dataset offers a reproducible organisational frame for further workforce research. These counts do not establish active training capacity, workforce shortage or population-adjusted inequity; those questions require additional programme-period, student-flow, employment and need data.

## Six-Month Change and Follow-up Patterns in AbilityScore During Routine Paediatric Developmental Care in India: Protocol for the PINNACLE-TRAJ Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study
https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/publications/zenodo-22761832.html
PINNACLE-TRAJ study protocol — preprint
Author-written abstract
Background: Repeated developmental assessments collected during routine care can describe change and gaps in reassessment across a service network. Their interpretation depends on comparable measurement over time and inclusion of children who do not return. A clearly defined cohort and transparent analysis of missing follow-up are needed to characterize changes in AbilityScore, a developmental index recorded in paediatric services.

Objective: To estimate mean change in AbilityScore between baseline and a prespecified six-month assessment window in a baseline-defined cohort, and to describe the availability and characteristics of follow-up. Secondary objectives concern longer-term scores, recorded developmental domains and associations with baseline characteristics.

Methods: PINNACLE-TRAJ is a planned retrospective observational study of routine records from eligible Pinnacle Blooms Network centres in India. The proposed database close is 30 June 2026. A documented comparable scoring era and eligible centres will be fixed from deployment and measurement records before outcome inspection. Children aged under 13 years at their first eligible baseline will enter the cohort without any requirement for a subsequent visit. Baselines must permit the full 150–210-day primary window; with the proposed close, the latest permissible baseline is 2 December 2025. The primary endpoint is the comparable score nearest day 180 within that window. Mean within-child change will be estimated with multilevel multiple imputation under a stated missing-at-random assumption and centre-aware uncertainty. Observed-case, weighting and missing-not-at-random analyses will assess sensitivity. Postbaseline care exposure will not define cohort membership or the primary contrast.

Results: Ethics review, study registration and selection of the final scoring era are pending. The eligible cohort size will be established after the required approvals and deployment review. This protocol reports the planned study; results are not yet available for publication.

Conclusions: The study is intended to describe score change and reassessment patterns within an eligible service population. Its uncontrolled design cannot estimate treatment effectiveness, isolate an AI contribution, establish an important clinical difference or provide population developmental norms.

## Concurrent Validity, Test-Retest Reliability, and Preliminary Minimal Clinically Important Difference of PinnacleAI AbilityScore: A Cross-Sectional Psychometric Validation Study Protocol
https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/publications/zenodo-19482476.html
Psychometric validation protocol — preprint
Author-written abstract
Background: AbilityScore is a standardized composite developmental index (0–1000) that quantifies child developmental performance relative to age-normed expectations. Operational data from more than 18.6 million therapy sessions show inter-rater reliability r = 0.91 and ICC = 0.88. However, formal concurrent validity against established reference instruments, controlled test-retest reliability, and minimal clinically important difference (MCID) have not been published.

Objective: To determine the concurrent validity of AbilityScore against Vineland-3, CARS-2, Bayley-4, and ABAS-3; to assess the reliability of the 7-day test-retest; and to estimate a preliminary MCID.

Methods: Cross-sectional multi-center psychometric validation study with a nested prospective test-retest substudy. Component A: n = 300 children aged 7 months to 7 years assessed with AbilityScore and comparator instruments in the same session by blinded raters in 6 Pinnacle Blooms Network centers. Component B: n = 60 subset, reassessed at 7 days. Primary analysis: Pearson correlation (Bonferroni-adjusted α = 0.017). Pre-registered SAP on OSF.

Discussion: This study addresses the single most important evidence gap for AbilityScore. It will determine whether the instrument meets the accepted thresholds for concurrent validity (r ≥ 0.50) and reliability (ICC ≥ 0.80), allowing the progression from operational evidence to formal psychometric validation.

Trial registration: CTRI (to be registered prior to first enrollment). OSF pre-registration of SAP (to be completed prior to data collection).

## AbilityScore: Development and Preliminary Psychometric Characterization of a Standardized Composite Index for Quantifying Child Developmental Readiness
https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/publications/zenodo-19482123.html
Methodology and preliminary psychometrics — preprint
Author-written abstract
Background: Since the late nineteenth century, developmental assessment has relied on a series of siloed instruments rather than a single developmental score. A child assessed with ADOS-2, Vineland and Bayley receives three separate reports on three incompatible scales, leaving families and clinicians without a unified picture of progress.

Objective: To describe the architecture, computation methodology, and preliminary psychometric evidence for AbilityScore, a standardized composite developmental index (0–1000) that quantifies observed functional developmental performance relative to age-normed expectations in multiple validated constructs.

Methods: AbilityScore synthesizes the clinical essence of 25 internationally validated assessments into a single metric, mapping 339 skills across 148 abilities through structured clinical observations. The scoring algorithm uses a Skill Index (60%) and Ability Index (40%) weighted composite with age-gender normalization. Seven domain-specific Readiness Indexes (Speech, Motor, Behaviour, Cognitive, School, Self-Sufficiency, Mainstream) provide multidimensional profiling. Preliminary psychometric evidence comes from operational data from approximately 18.6 million therapy sessions spanning more than 70 centers, 4 Indian states, 16 languages, and 28 diagnostic categories.

Results: Operational data show inter-rater reliability r = 0.91 (p < 0.001), intraclass correlation coefficient ICC = 0.88 (95% CI 0.84–0.91), mean absolute percentage error MAPE = 6.7%, and bias variance ratio ≤ 1.05. These real-world scoring consistency metrics from routine operations across more than 70 centers provide a robust operational foundation for the formal validation study now in planning, but do not substitute for controlled psychometric validation.

Conclusions: AbilityScore is a scientifically structured, WHO ICF-aligned composite index for developmental measurement. Formal concurrent validity testing against Vineland-3, CARS-2, and Bayley-4, along with test-retest reliability studies, are now in planning (BHCL-VAL-2026-001). This monograph documents the instrument in sufficient detail to support the upcoming validation studies, regulatory submissions, and clinical use.

## Pinnacle Global Autism Framework (PGAF): India's First Validated, Scalable, Outcome-Based Child Development System
https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/publications/zenodo-15487405.html
Institution-authored framework report
Author-supplied repository description
This whitebook presents 12 formal research studies comprising India’s first nationally validated, scalable, and outcome-driven autism care framework. Developed under the Pinnacle Global Research Consortium, the Pinnacle Global Autism Framework (PGAF) integrates five patented systems — AbilityScore®, TherapeuticAI®, SEVA™, Everyday Therapy™, and TherapySphere™.

Together, these systems have been validated across over 19 million therapy sessions in 70+ Indian cities, leading to outcome improvements in behavior, sensory regulation, speech, and school readiness. This whitebook is intended to support governments, educators, therapists, and global development agencies working to implement measurable, ethical child development systems aligned with SDG 3, SDG 4, and SDG 10.

Originally submitted to SSRN, this version is preserved in Zenodo as the open-access, archival edition for permanent citation. Indexed on ORCID and Google Scholar. Patents filed under Indian IP registry support core systems described.

## Meaningful Change in Childhood Participation: A Systematic Review Protocol for Child- and Caregiver-Anchored Estimates in Neurodevelopmental Disability
https://pinnacle-verify.saripalli.chatgpt.site/evidence/publications/zenodo-22827813.html
Systematic-review protocol — preprint; unregistered
Author-written abstract
Background: A change in participation score does not establish whether children or caregivers consider it important. Published estimates may represent different constructs, reporters and statistical quantities, limiting their use as individual decision thresholds.

Objective: To identify and appraise child- or caregiver-anchored estimates of important change in childhood participation, distinguish their interpretations, and map evidence gaps.

Methods: Eligible longitudinal studies will derive, evaluate or explicitly attempt an important-change estimate for participation attendance or involvement among children with a prespecified neurodevelopmental condition who are younger than 18 years at baseline. Later assessments crossing age 18 will be retained and flagged. Searches are planned in PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, ERIC and ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global, supplemented by citation, registry and preprint searching. Two human reviewers will independently select reports, extract data and appraise estimates. The analysis unit is an estimate or documented failed attempt within a study family. Participation content, anchor, reporter and estimand will be coded separately. Individual responder thresholds, anchor-defined mean change and longitudinal group contrasts will retain distinct interpretations. An adapted domain-level appraisal will assess respondent alignment, anchor relevance, association with target change, precision and the importance represented by the anchor contrast. The co-primary outputs are an estimate catalogue and an evidence-gap and credibility map. Narrative synthesis will preserve instrument scales and study dependence; meta-analysis is not planned.

Discussion: The review will distinguish supported interpretations from uncertainty and missing evidence, including if few estimates are eligible. It may guide future anchor studies; it will not establish proprietary-instrument validity or treatment effectiveness.

Registration: PROSPERO submission is planned before formal screening, subject to eligibility and completion of the required declarations. No identifier has been assigned.

## The Voice of the Unheard
